text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- At the meeting of the European Union summit in Dublin Prime Minister Andris Shkele spoke about Latvia's achievements in fighting illegal immigration, securing the country's borders and economic achievements.
- The fifth congress of the Latvian Christian Democratic Union decided against merging with the right-wing nationalist party Fatherland and Freedom.
- The State Statistics Committee said Latvia's GDP increased 2.3 percent in the first nine months of 1996.
- The Latvian government is considering a 25 percent reduction of the property tax which is to be partly compensated by increasing land tax.

- There is a difference of almost $40 million between losses of the Latvian Shipping company counted by the international auditor Coopers & Lybrand, and those calculated in accordance with national accountancy law. The Latvian Privatisation Agency has so far received seven applications to privatise the Latvian Shipping company ahead of its December 20 deadline.
- An equivalent of 8.2 million lats has been allocated within the framework of the EU Phare programme to support economic reforms in Latvia.

- The German timber trading company Baltic Holz Grosshandel has warned the Latvian forestry and lumber products trade association that the Latvian government's plans to cut export tariffs on logs could lead to the group withdrawing from the Latvian market.
